strengths: The mean-point construction is a simple, original, and useful contribution to a difficult multiview geometry problem. Generating an approximate fifth correspondence allows established five-point and P3P solvers to address four-point three-view pose estimation, substantially reducing implementation complexity compared with specialized alternatives.

The empirical evaluation is substantial: 90,000 triplets across 18 scenes and three datasets, with both PoseLib and GC-RANSAC. The supplement includes noise, camera geometry, outlier, threshold, and component ablations. Evaluation using errors from all three camera pairs strengthens the evidence beyond the main paper's metric.

Accuracy improvements remain after strengthening the five-point baseline. In Table 2, 4p3v(M±δ)+R+F+ENM achieves PhotoTourism AUC@10 of 77.14, compared with 76.20 for 5pt+P3P+R+F+ENM and 73.53 for the homotopy solver. Consistent aggregate improvements across datasets support the practical contribution.

The manuscript explains why early refitting, fourth-point refinement, and filtering make approximate hypotheses useful within RANSAC. Held-out parameter validation, detailed experimental settings, and a source-code link provide a credible basis for reproduction. These strengths favor acceptance despite the reservations below.
weaknesses: The runtime comparison with the homotopy baseline is materially confounded by initialization. Section 8.3, footnote 8 reports approximately 45 ms for loading its data once per RANSAC run, substantial relative to the reported end-to-end runtimes. Repeated triplet estimation could amortize this cost. Table 4 also reports a faster standalone HC solver than either mean-point solver. The evidence therefore supports the accuracy advantage more convincingly than the claimed speed advantage over HC.

The strongest speed–accuracy claims are not fully established against the enhanced five-point baseline. Figure 4 omits its +R+F variants, although Table 2 shows that these modifications substantially improve it. The most accurate proposed variant gains 0.94 PhotoTourism AUC@10 points over the fully enhanced baseline while taking 112.60 versus 56.52 ms. Matched-runtime curves for that stronger baseline are needed to establish the claimed best trade-off.

The theoretical analysis gives limited guidance about failure conditions. The mean-point epipolar bound scales with triangle size and does not bound pose error or ensure successful refinement. The synthetic results demonstrate approximation bias even without image noise and deterioration under larger viewing angles. Consequently, the statement that ENM makes scene dependence negligible is stronger than the established analysis, although the empirical robustness evidence is valuable.

The real-data protocol retains only correspondences consistently matched across all three views and requires at least ten matches. This does not evaluate the comparative behavior under partial visibility, where the (5,5,3) baseline can exploit additional two-view-only matches. The demonstrated advantage should therefore be scoped to the tested triplet-track setting.
